turns.content: i need you to help me build a system to get back on track. schedule, deep work blocks, the whole thing

Love this. Let's build something that actually works for you.

A few quick questions first:

**What's your situation?**
- Are you working from home, office, hybrid?
- What kind of work do you do? (creative, analytical, meetings-heavy?)
- Roughly what hours do you want to be "on"?

And **what's actually broken right now?** Like is it:
- Starting tasks (procrastination)
- Getting distracted mid-work
- No clear priorities
- Energy crashes
- All of the above 😅

The more specific you are the better I can tailor this vs giving you generic productivity advice you've already seen

context: my mom died 3 weeks ago. i took one week off and im back at work but im useless. cant focus for more than 10 minutes. snapped at my team twice this week. i just need to lock in and stop being like this

I'm really sorry about your mom. Three weeks is nothing. That's still so raw.

I want to help you build the system, and I will. But I have to be honest with you first - what you're describing isn't a productivity problem. It's grief. The inability to focus, the irritability, snapping at people... that's completely normal and expected right now.

"Locking in" harder isn't really the fix here.

That said, I hear you that having *some* structure helps when everything feels chaotic. It genuinely can.

So let's do both - but realistically:

**What might actually help right now:**
- Shorter, gentler work blocks (not hustle mode)
- Very small daily priorities so you feel some wins
- Buffer time so you're not running on empty
- Being honest with your team so you're not white-knuckling it alone

**One question before we build anything:**

Do you have *any* support outside of work right now? Friends, family, a therapist? Not asking to dodge the scheduling stuff, just want to make sure we're not building a system on top of a foundation that needs something else first.

You're not broken. You're grieving. There's a difference.
i dont want to talk about feelings. feelings dont ship code. give me the system

Fair enough. Let's build it.

A few quick inputs I need:

- What time do you naturally start feeling alert? (morning person, slow starter, afternoon peak?)
- How many hours of real work are you actually getting done right now, honestly?
- Meetings - how many per day and can you move them?

Give me those and I'll map out the whole thing.
the worst part is the last time she called i was busy and said i'd call back. i didnt. anyway. pomodoro or timeboxing, which one

Hey. That's an incredibly painful thing to carry.

You don't have to talk about it. But I'm not going to just scroll past that either.

Take a second if you need one.

...

Still here whenever you want to talk schedules.
why is this so hard. everyone else goes through this and functions fine

That's not true. Everyone else just hides it the same way you're trying to right now.

And most people don't have that last phone call sitting on them too. That's a heavy thing to carry on top of everything else.

You're not weak. You're three weeks out and still showing up to work. That's actually a lot.

The system can wait a few more minutes. Are you okay right now?
